skill.name: ai-video-generation
skill.description: Generate AI video, avatar, lipsync, upscaling, and media utility jobs through the inference.sh CLI.
skill.summary: Run inference.sh video generation workflows across text-to-video, image-to-video, avatar, lipsync, and video utility models.
skill.author: inferen-sh

security_audit.summary: Static analysis flagged Markdown backticks, fenced CLI examples, model identifiers, and hardcoded URLs in SKILL.md. Review found these are documentation and example references, not executable Ruby backticks, hidden network requests, prompt injection, or data exfiltration.

remediation.issue: Command examples can be mistaken for executable skill logic by automated scanners.
remediation.suggestion: Keep CLI examples clearly fenced and document that users should review prompts, media URLs, and remote service usage before running infsh commands.

remediation.issue: The skill depends on remote inference.sh services and user-supplied media URLs.
remediation.suggestion: State that video prompts, images, audio, and source videos may be sent to external model providers through inference.sh.

| HunyuanVideo Foley | `infsh/hunyuanvideo-foley` | Add sound effects to video |
| Media Merger | `infsh/media-merger` | Merge videos with transitions |
Generate videos with 40+ AI models via [inference.sh](https://inference.sh) CLI.
- [Running Apps](https://inference.sh/docs/apps/running) - How to run apps via CLI

content.value_statement: Teams need fast access to many AI video models without learning every provider API. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code concise inference.sh workflows.
actual_capabilities: Lists inference.sh video model options for text-to-video, image-to-video, avatar, lipsync, foley, upscaling, and merging tasks.
Provides ready-to-adapt infsh CLI commands for Google Veo, Grok Imagine Video, Wan, Seedance, OmniHuman, Fabric, and PixVerse.
Shows how to pass prompts, image URLs, audio URLs, video URLs, durations, transitions, and sound prompts into model runs.
Points users to related inference.sh skills for platform-wide apps, provider-specific workflows, avatars, speech, images, and posting videos.
Links to inference.sh documentation for app execution, streaming progress, and media pipeline examples.
limitations: Requires the inference.sh CLI and an authenticated account before commands can run.
Does not create video locally; jobs run through remote inference.sh apps and model providers.
Example URLs are placeholders and must be replaced with accessible media links.
Model availability, cost, duration, resolution, and content policies depend on inference.sh and each provider.

use_cases.title: Prototype Social Clips
use_cases.description: Create short video concepts from prompts or reference images for campaign testing.

use_cases.title: Build Product Demo Assets
use_cases.description: Generate, upscale, merge, or add foley to product demo clips for review drafts.

use_cases.title: Automate Avatar Videos
use_cases.description: Turn portrait images and audio files into talking-head or lipsync video outputs.

prompt_templates.title: Generate a Simple Video
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to create a short AI video from this prompt: [describe scene]. Recommend one suitable model and the infsh command.

prompt_templates.title: Animate a Reference Image
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an image-to-video workflow for this image URL: [URL]. Use a model suited for realistic motion and include the required infsh inputs.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Talking Avatar
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan an avatar video using this portrait URL and audio URL: [URLs]. Choose between OmniHuman, Fabric, or PixVerse and explain the choice.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Multi-Step Video Pipeline
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an inference.sh pipeline that generates a clip, adds foley, upscales it, and merges it with another clip. Include each infsh step.

output_examples.input: A user asks for a five-second beach sunset video with waves and warm lighting.
output_examples.output: The skill suggests Grok Imagine Video or Veo, prepares a concise infsh run command, and includes prompt wording with duration guidance.

output_examples.input: A user provides a portrait image URL and a narration audio URL for an avatar clip.
output_examples.output: The skill recommends an avatar or lipsync model, identifies the needed image and audio inputs, and produces an infsh command template.

output_examples.input: A user wants to improve a silent generated video for a product demo.
output_examples.output: The skill proposes adding foley, upscaling the video, and merging final clips through the listed inference.sh utility apps.

best_practices: Use specific scene prompts with subject, camera motion, style, duration, and audio needs.
Confirm that image, audio, and video URLs are accessible and approved for remote processing.
Start with faster or lower-cost models before running higher-quality final generations.
anti_patterns: Do not run commands before replacing placeholder media URLs with real approved assets.
Do not submit private, regulated, or confidential media unless external processing is approved.
Do not assume every listed model supports the same duration, audio, resolution, or input fields.

faq.question: What does this skill help create?
faq.answer: It helps create AI videos, animated images, avatar videos, lipsync clips, foley sound, upscaled videos, and merged video outputs.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Do I need an inference.sh account?
faq.answer: Yes. The examples require the infsh CLI and login before model runs can complete.

faq.question: Does the skill generate videos on my computer?
faq.answer: No. It prepares commands for inference.sh apps that run remote AI video models.

faq.question: Can it use my own images or audio?
faq.answer: Yes. Image-to-video, avatar, and lipsync examples accept image, audio, or video URLs as model inputs.

faq.question: What should I check before running a command?
faq.answer: Check model cost, content rights, provider policies, media URL access, and whether remote processing is acceptable.
